title: Grade 7 Math — Thu, May 21
description: Probability — Day 4 of 5: Complementary events and experimental probability
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What is the complementary event of 'rolling a 6 on a die'?
questions.explanation: Complementary = the event that 'rolling 6' does NOT occur = getting 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

questions.question: P(getting at least one tail) when a coin is tossed twice = ?
questions.explanation: P(at least one T) = 1 − P(no tail) = 1 − P(HH) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.question: A coin is tossed 100 times and lands Head 43 times. What is the experimental probability of Head?
questions.explanation: Experimental P(H) = number of heads ÷ total trials = 43/100.

questions.question: If P(A) = 0.4, what is P(not A)?
A die is rolled 60 times. Theoretically, how many times should we expect a '3'?
P(drawing a card that is NOT an Ace from a 52-card deck)?
A bag has 12 balls. 4 are green. What is P(not green)?
A fair coin is tossed 200 times. Expected number of Tails?
A die is rolled 120 times. How many times is an even number expected?
What is the relationship between experimental and theoretical probability?
options: Experimental probability approaches theoretical probability as trials increase
Experimental is always less than theoretical
questions.explanation: As the number of trials increases, experimental probability gets closer to theoretical probability (Law of Large Numbers).

questions.question: P(getting sum > 10 when rolling two dice)?
In 40 spins of a 4-colour spinner, red was expected 10 times. How many green?
questions.explanation: 4 equal sectors, so each colour expected = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 times.

questions.question: P(selecting a vowel from the word MATHEMATICS)?
questions.explanation: MATHEMATICS has 11 letters: M,A,T,H,E,M,A,T,I,C,S. Vowels: A,E,A,I = 4. P(vowel) = 4/11.
